title: CLI command catalog audit
description:
Verify every CLI/storage/structure/semantics claim in `docs/reference/cli-commands.md` against current source and fix all drift class-wide.

## Background

`docs/reference/cli-commands.md` (3,819 lines) is the CLI command catalog, audited as its own footprint — isolated by size — within an exhaustive, source-verified documentation audit of the adopter-facing documentation surface. The scope is the exhaustive audit of the existing catalog content. Recurring drift classes to sweep for include invented CLI surface, stale storage-format specifics, over-credited guarantees, legacy or future narration, and prerequisite/environment drift.

One live drift instance is already known and must be fixed: `cli-commands.md:3756-3757` documents the event type `state_changed` with a `new_state` field; the real event tag is `issue_state_changed` and the real field is `to`. This is a seed, not the full defect set — sweeping the whole file for every instance of each drift class found is this work's job.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Every documented command and flag in `docs/reference/cli-commands.md` exists in the current generated CLI schema or the current clap definitions.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every repository-relative link, heading anchor, source citation, and addressable-item citation in `docs/reference/cli-commands.md` resolves.
- [hard] REQ-03: Every diagram-shaped block in `docs/reference/cli-commands.md` is Mermaid; directory trees and verbatim command output are not diagrams.
- [hard] REQ-04: Every factual claim in `docs/reference/cli-commands.md` about CLI behavior, storage layout, repository structure, or engine semantics matches the current source tree; where a drift instance is found, its whole class is swept across the footprint, not patched line-by-line.
- [hard] REQ-05: Prose in `docs/reference/cli-commands.md` states current behavior only — no legacy or future/roadmap narration remains.
- [hard] REQ-06: Every volatile fact in `docs/reference/cli-commands.md` with an existing projection or citation surface is projected or cited rather than hand-copied; each volatile fact with no such surface is cited to its source file and recorded for follow-up filing.
- [hard] REQ-07: `cli-commands.md:3756-3757`'s event-query example cites the real event tag (`issue_state_changed`) and the real field name (`to`), not `state_changed`/`new_state`.

## Notes

The linked plan document carries the exact check commands and expected outputs (§2).

CLI-surface verification must use a binary built from the current HEAD; a stale installed binary has previously produced false verification results. The generated CLI schema under-reports the real flag surface (clap `visible_alias` flag forms and the global flags are absent from it), so a documented flag absent from the schema is checked against the clap definitions in `crates/jit/src/cli.rs` before being declared invented; only a flag absent from both is a defect.

No box-drawing content is expected in this footprint on the current tree; any found is adjudicated against the directory-tree/verbatim-output carve-out before conversion.

A doc in this footprint found wholly obsolete or redundant may be deleted or merged into another, with the rationale recorded on this task. Every inbound link tree-wide is repointed in the same change — links are uniformly relative markdown, so inbound references are findable by filename in both bare-name and relative-path forms — and no doc is removed before its inbound links are repointed. After any deletion or merge, every link and anchor tree-wide still resolves.

Blast radius: single file.
